Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Wheezing for 2 days, progressively worsening, especially at night
- Associated symptoms: Shortness of breath, difficulty completing sentences while speaking; denies chest pain, dizziness
- Recent trigger: Wheezing started after cleaning the house and possible dust exposure
- Past medical history: Childhood asthma (mostly resolved), occasional hay fever in summer
- Previous treatment: Has used an asthma inhaler in the past, inhaler last used a couple of months ago; has previously taken steroids for asthma
- Medications: Asthma inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented); no current use of antihistamines
- Allergies: None known
- Social history: Not documented

Objective:
- No physical examination findings documented
- No vital signs recorded
- No investigations performed during consultation

Assessment & Plan:

1. Wheezing and shortness of breath
   - Assessment or likely diagnosis: Possible asthma exacerbation or allergy-related airway reactivity
   - Differential diagnosis: Asthma exacerbation, allergy to dust
   - Investigations planned: Pulse oximetry (oxygen saturation) at clinic; further tests to determine if symptoms are due to asthma or allergy
   - Treatment planned: Recommendation to take an antihistamine if available (none at home, advised to obtain over the counter or obtain prescription at the clinic); possible steroid treatment depending on clinic assessment
   - Relevant referrals: Letter to GP for in-person review and further management

Quality checks:
●	Missing but clinically expected elements: Physical examination findings (including auscultation), vital signs (especially oxygen saturation, respiratory rate), detailed medication list (including inhaler type, dose/frequency), social history, smoking status, documentation of asthma control, peak flow measurement.
●	Internal conflicts: None noted.
●	Transcript quality: Clear; no major inaudible sections.
